subject: physics
question_text: Mention the methods used to decrease friction.

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), Unit 5 SHORT ANSWER. The mark split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher; no exam appearance years are printed for this question, so appearances[] stays empty.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: Polishing
lines: lock into each other, so friction falls.
steps.margin_note: Give the method a number and a one-line reason. The reason is what earns the mark.
steps.why: Friction comes from surface roughness meshing together. Take the roughness away and there is less to mesh.
common_mistakes: Naming the four methods with no reason for any of them.

recall.must_convey: That polishing smooths the surfaces and reduces friction.

steps.label: Ball bearings
lines: Hard steel balls placed between moving
parts turn sliding friction into rolling
steps.margin_note: The words that earn this are "sliding into rolling". Say which becomes which.
steps.why: A rolling ball never drags across the surface — a fresh point touches down each moment instead of scraping.
common_mistakes: Saying bearings "remove friction". They replace it with a much smaller kind.

recall.must_convey: That ball bearings turn sliding friction into much smaller rolling friction.
accept: ball bearings change sliding to rolling friction
sliding friction rolling friction ga marutundi

steps.label: Lubricants
lines: Oil or grease fills the hollows and
keeps the two surfaces apart, so they
slide over a fluid layer instead.
steps.margin_note: Say the surfaces are kept APART. That is the whole mechanism.
steps.why: Once a fluid film separates them the solids never touch, and a liquid layer shears far more easily than metal on metal.
common_mistakes: Writing only "oil is applied" with no explanation of what the oil does.

recall.must_convey: That a lubricant fills the gaps and keeps the surfaces apart.

steps.label: Streamlining
lines: Cars, aeroplanes and ships are given
curved shapes so that air or water
steps.margin_note: Name the friction being reduced — this one is air or water friction, not surface friction.
steps.why: The first three methods attack solid-on-solid contact. This one attacks a different opponent entirely: the fluid the body moves through.
common_mistakes: Describing streamlining as a way to reduce friction with the ROAD.

recall.must_convey: That streamlined shapes reduce the friction from air or water.
accept: curved shapes so air flows smoothly
